correctness.rationale: PASS: On additive Sym_n(F_q), character orthogonality yields chi-square Σ_nontrivial |μ̂|^{2t}. Odd q characters correspond to symmetric quadratic forms A, whose rank-r Gauss-sum magnitude squared is q^(−r); count of rank-r forms is B_q(n,r) q^{r(r+1)/2} H_q(ceil r/2), giving (1). In characteristic two, use all homogeneous quadratic characters rather than the degenerate trace pairing; a polar alternating form of rank 2r contributes q^{2r} radical-vanishing refinements with squared character magnitude q^(−2r). Counting polar forms gives B_q(n,2r) q^{r(2r+1)} H_q(r) and (2) for t>=1; t=0 is separately point mass. Gaussian coefficient asymptotics and q^{-r²/2} domination yield both fixed-offset series. Above n+a, chi-square controls TV; below n−a, rank≤t and a union bound over kernel a-planes give TV→1. Independently enumerated all q=2,n=2 symmetric-matrix states and exact rank-one convolution through t=4; chi-square 1,1/4,1/16,1/64 agrees. Finite checks complement the all-n Fourier proof.
